info.title: Workbench Swagger
info.description: Every HTTP endpoint the Workbench's own backend exposes (`agent-service/src/admin/server.ts`) — the tools this platform runs on. This documents the PLATFORM itself, not any target system under test — for a discovered target's own API, see the Analysis tab's "API Inventory" diagram instead. Hand-authored from the real route handlers; `checkOpenApiCoverage.ts` catches drift between this file and the real routes. This is a local, single-user dev tool with no auth of its own — every route here executes for real, exactly as calling it with curl would.

post.summary: Deploy a target from its docker-compose component

200.description: Streams newline-delimited JSON progress lines while the operation runs: `{"type":"progress","message":"..."}` for each step, then a final line — `{"type":"done","projectName":"...","ports":[...]}` — or `{"type":"error","error":"..."}` on failure. swagger-ui's Execute button genuinely calls this route (same-origin) but shows the whole buffered response only once the connection closes, not line-by-line as it streams — a known cosmetic limitation of documenting a live stream in OpenAPI 3.0, which has no native way to describe one.

post.description: Also restores the live descriptor/corrections/UAT (backing up whatever is currently live first, into archive/pre-restore-.../) and additively restores historical discovery-report/grouping/approved-spec/analytics files that are missing locally. Does not restore setup-script.ts (a container filesystem write there can never actually persist — see this route's own extensive comment in server.ts) or test-env.env (a resolved view, not the raw sidecar).

delete.description: No trash/undo — a real `rm -rf`. Refuses on git-tracked (shared demo) snapshots.

post.summary: Run the k6 backend/API load test for a target

200.description: Streams newline-delimited JSON progress lines while the operation runs: `{"type":"progress","message":"..."}` for each step, then a final line — `{"type":"done","exitCode":number,"passed":bool}` — a nonzero exit means k6's own thresholds failed, a legitimate load-test outcome, not necessarily an infrastructure error — or `{"type":"error","error":"..."}` on failure. swagger-ui's Execute button genuinely calls this route (same-origin) but shows the whole buffered response only once the connection closes, not line-by-line as it streams — a known cosmetic limitation of documenting a live stream in OpenAPI 3.0, which has no native way to describe one.

post.description: HTTP-only load against the descriptor's own rest-api component, no browser involved — resolves the base URL the same way Discovery does. Needs an already-approved <descriptor>-load.js.
